text: Dunder methods let your own objects work with Python's built-in operators, like plus and double-equals.
Defining dunder-add tells Python what the plus sign should do between two of your objects.
Here adding two vectors returns a new vector with their components summed.
[chuckle] So a plus b just works, reading exactly like the math it represents.
dunder-eq defines what double-equals means, letting you compare objects by value instead of identity.
[sniff] Without it, Python would only check if two objects are literally the same one in memory.
Now two separate vectors with the same numbers count as equal, which is usually what you want.
[sigh] There are dunders for subtraction, multiplication, less-than, indexing — nearly every operator Python has.
[groan] Operator overloading, used tastefully, makes your custom types feel like a natural part of the language.
Up next, abstract classes. Comment PYTHON if you want the cheat sheet.
